headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 14 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: Another mountain showdown is on the cards today with relentless ups and downs from Jaén all the way to the summit finish at Sierra de la Pandera: 154.5 km of racing, 4,338 metres of elevation gain! Who will succeed Richard Carapaz, the winner here in 2022? The neutral start is set at 13:15, the start proper at 13:33 after a 7.4 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Welcome to Jaén
subtext: Jaén first hosted a La Vuelta stage in 1976 (Theo Smit won stage 3) and most recently in 2021, when stage 12 headed to Cordoba. Denmark’s Magnus Cort took the fifth of his six La Vuelta stage wins. Jaén is José Manuel Diaz Gallego’s hometown. The Burgos Burpellet BH climber takes part in his third La Vuelta. Ha achieved his best result two days ago with an 11th place at Calar Alto. This year, he’s won the Classica Terres de l’Ebre on roads visited by La Vuelta 26 on stage 5.

headline: A province made for cycling
subtext: The province of Jaén waited for the 1976 edition to host La Vuelta but it has become a modern staple of the race. Today marks the 22nd start and 20th finish in the province that has been missing on the map of La Vuelta only five times since 2006. On the last occasion, two years ago, stage 7 of La Vuelta 24 went from Ubeda to Cazorla, where Primoz Roglic won a 2-man uphill sprint against Enric Mas. Mattias Skjelmose was 5th and Harold Tejada finished 7th after he took part in the breakaway. The province of Jaén is often visited by the Vuelta a Andalucia - last February, stage 3 started from Jaén and went to Lopera, where Milan Fretin won the sprint and Ivan Romeo kept the leader’s jersey en route to his overall victory. It is also home of the Clasica Jaén Paraiso Interior since 2022. Among the participants in La Vuelta 26, Ivan Romeo, Pello Bilbao and Attila Valter finished in the top 10 last February. Jordan Labrosse, Axel Laurance, Clément Berthet, Carlos Canal, Bastien Tronchon, Sepp Kuss, Andreas Kron, Lorenzo Rota, and Lennard Kämna also achieved top 10 results in previous editions.

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 7.4 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Yesterday brought no change at the top of the GC: Enric Mas (Movistar) remains a solid leader ahead of Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM), Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost), and Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos). Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek) made the most of the 43-an breakaway to gain over two minutes on his GC rivals. He’s still 7th overall, but has brought the gap down to 5’32’’.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Yesterday, Wout van Aert took his 15th Grand Tour stage win (10 in the Tour, 4 in La Vuelta, 1 in the Giro) and received his 20th green jersey as leader of the points standings of La Vuelta (13 in 2024, 7 in 2026). He also has 20 green jerseys at the Tour de France, where he won the points standings in 2022. Van Aert is up to 224 points. His Visma-Lease a Bike teammate Matthew Brennan follows with 159 points after he finished 3rd yesterday. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) completes the top 3 with 96 points. Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) has 94.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) made the breakaway again, bringing his tally up to 58 points, but Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) was also at the front and slightly reduced the different at the top of the mountains standings - he trails by 18 points. Enric Mas (Movistar) follows with 24 points.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) still leads the young riders standings with a gap of 30’’ to Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) and 9’07’’ to Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM), who was in the breakaway yesterday.

headline: Team standings
subtext: Decathlon CMA CGM face today’s challenges with a lead of 1h07’36’’ to Bahrain Victorious and 1h11’13’’ to Netcompany Ineos.

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility) will race with a distinctive bib as he was named the most combative rider yesterday.

headline: Diaz Gallego: "Jaén has always been right behind me and behind cycling"
subtext: Hailing from Jaén, José Manuel Díaz Gallego (Burgos-BH-Burpellet) is racing at home today: “It’s a wonderful feeling. With all the spectators cheering us on, it really gives you a huge boost. Without a doubt, being in La Vuelta a España is already one of the best moments [of my career], so just imagine if a stage starts at home and finishes at home. Few things could be better! I’ve always received a lot of support from home; Jaén has always been right behind me and behind cycling, so today I hope they’ll cheer me on, especially on the final climb, and that I’ll have strong legs. First of all, we’re going to try to be in the breakaway. Hopefully we’ll be there, and if we are, we’ll try to put the pieces together to make it a good stage. There are lots of climbs; we don’t know which one will break up the peloton, but without a doubt, the finish on the Sierra de la Pandera is quite tough. There, I reckon everyone will climb one by one, and there’ll be quite a few gaps today.”

headline: How will Oliveira celebrate his birthday?
subtext: Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG) was in the breakaway for his birthday last year, on the way to L’Angliru, where his teammate and compatriot Joao Almeida won. Will he do it again today as he turns 30? "Why not? We are only four riders, this stage will be quite open and I think the breakaway can arrive. It's not the kind of finish for me but who knows? Last year it was not my kind of finish but I went in the breakaway and I still helped the team, so maybe yes, I could be in the breakaway with other teammates. I don't have a lot of teammates but we'll try our best. Joao [Almeida] is good, he's not having the best year but he's a fighter, he’s mentally a strong rider and we have to support him. He showed the other day in the breakaway that the legs are there, he just has to have a good day and everything can change. He’s proving to everyone that he can still be in the fight, and I think today, tomorrow and the next week he’s gonna show us that he still has very good legs."

headline: Stage 14 is ON!
subtext: It's time to battle it out on Jaén's mountains!

headline: The battle for the break is on
subtext: Nine riders have opened a small gap at km 3.

headline: A massive group on the move
subtext: Now it's around 30 riders at the front!

headline: Back together
subtext: The attackers are reeled in at km 5. It should be quite a battle before the break gets away.

headline: 24 attackers on the move
subtext: They've set off at km 9.

headline: Back together again
subtext: Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS Astana) is among the contenders for today's breakaway: “Yesterday, the feeling was good at the start, but maybe in the end I suffered a bit with the hot temperatures. For me, today and the next week are really good. But I want to think about today and this summit finish, one of the last this week, so I want to stay in front. I try to go the breakaway and it can arrive for sure. There will be for sure a battle for GC, but in the first part I’ll be in the front and after we’ll see.”

headline: The battle goes on
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) is already active at the front of the race. Meanwhile, his compatriot Juan Guillermo Martinez (Picnic PostNL) returns to the peloton after a mechanical.

headline: Hugo Houle abandons

subtext: And the bunch splits due to the high pace.

headline: 35 seconds between the first two groups

headline: An impressive break

Pello Bilbao and Santiago Butirago (Bahrain Victorious) have also made the break, as well as Clément Berthet and Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United), Lorenzo Fortunato and Cristian Rodriguez (XDS Astana)... headline: 41.8 km covered in the first hour
subtext: It has been a very hard battle on demanding terrain.

headline: Berthet and Rodriguez are the main GC contenders at the front
subtext: Clément Berthet (Groupama-FDJ United) and Cristian Rodriguez (XDS Astana) are respectively 10th (+11'06'') and 11th (+11'10'') in the overall standings after they already made the breakaway yesterday. They're curretnly 3'20'' ahead of the peloton with the breakaway.

headline: The gap is stable: three and a half minutes
subtext: The peloton are not willing to give much of a margin to such a strong group.

headline: Knowledge of the terrain can be key
subtext: In the breakaway, we find two riders who climbed to Sierra de la Pandera in 2017 and 2022: Julien Bernard (Lidl-Trek) and David de la Cruz (Pinarello Q36.5). “Today is going to be a very tough day, because of the heat and the finish at La Pandera, but I’ll try to get through the day as best I can, and see if I can soon get my body back on track and feel good again, because yesterday was the first day of La Vuelta that I felt quite good", De la Cruz said this morning. "I think we did the Pandera in 2017, and again in 2022, so I know the climb well. It’s a very tough climb, not just the climb itself, but the approach: going through Valdepeñas de Jaén, where the steep stretch is really tough, then a very wide road… and then the heat – today is probably the day when you’ll feel the heat the most.”

headline: Oliveira pulls the breakaway
subtext: UAE Emirates XRG's Portuguese baroudeur has made the breakaway on his 30th birthday, just like he raced at the front last year on September 5th. That day, La Vuelta headed to L'Angliru... and his compatriot and teammate Joao Almeida won the stage. He's also in the breakaway today.

headline: Aular and Canal set the pace in the peloton
subtext: The peloton trail by 3'45'' as they reach km 66.

headline: The gap increases
subtext: The peloton trail by 4'10'' after 69 kilometres.

headline: 10 kilometres to the first categorised climb of the day
subtext: The ascent of the Puerto de los Villares (a classic of the stages to Sierra de la Pandera) begins at km 82.3, but the route has been far from flat. The riders have already overcome around 1,500 metres of elevation.

headline: A mechanical for Mas?
subtext: The Spaniard stops on the right side of the road with his teammates. The gap will get over five minutes.

headline: The first climb of the day: Puerto de los Villares
subtext: The road rises for the attackers as they tackle 10.5 km of climbing at 5.4%. The peloton trail by 4'50'' with Enric Mas (Movsitar) back at the front.

headline: The peloton begin the ascent
subtext: Orluis Aular (Movistar) setsthe pace with a gap of 4'40''.

headline: Labrosse abandons
subtext: Jordan Labrosse is the second Decathlon CMA CGM to leave La Vuelta 26 after Gregor Mühlberger yesterday.

headline: Oliver Peace also abandons
subtext: Meanwhile, the attackers face the final 5 kilometres up the Puerto Los Villares.

headline: The gap decreases on the climb
subtext: The peloton have already moved 40'' closer to the break: 3'50''.

headline: Bilbao pulls the breakaway
subtext: Fortunato is on his wheel.

headline: The peloton has already gained back a minute
Martin-Guyonnet increases the pace with Berthet on his wheel
subtext: Their teammate Rudy Molard spoke this morning about the possibility to gain time in the overall standings through the breakaway, hoping other teams won't help Movistar control the day: "I’d have preferred Movistar to be the only ones riding at the back so they’d wear themselves out a bit. But you can see it’s a bit like it sometimes is in the third week of a Grand Tour, where the riders in the top five want to defend their positions, so the leader’s team always finds support. It’s a shame because yesterday there was a great opportunity to wear down the Movistar team.”

headline: Gall: "Mühlberger was so strong"
subtext: Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) spoke about losing Gregor Mühlberger at the start: "It is a real bummer, he was so strong and the most important guy on the climbs. He was also my roommate, so not just on the bike, but also off the bike he was bringing a good spirit, energy. Luckily he didn't hurt himself too badly, glad that nothing too bad happened but of course it’s a big loss. [We will] maybe be a bit more conservative, we still have a really strong team but everyone is getting pretty tired with the heat. I think today the stage allows us to wait a bit longer until the last 3-4 km where it really gets steep, there is no need to do anything crazy before that."

headline: Buitrago leads the way to the first summit of the day
subtext: Fortunato is second at the line. Buitrago all but secures the polka-dot jersey for another stage if he makes it to the finish without incidents.

headline: 50 kilometres to go for Vermaerke

headline: Memories from Sierra de la Pandera
subtext: Sierra de la Pandera was introduced in the 2002 edition of La Vuelta and returned in 2003, 2006, 2009, 2017 and 2022. Today marks the seventh finish at this summit. The last winner at Sierra de la Pandera is Richard Carapaz from the breakaway. Among the GC contenders, Primoz Roglic was the strongest and finished 28’’ ahead of Enric Mas and 48’’ ahead of La Roja wearer and eventual overall winner Remco Evenepoel.In 2022, the peloton tackled the Sierra de la Pandera climb from Los Villares while they face the Valdepeñas de Jaén side today, like in 2017, when Rafal Maja won the stage from the early breakaway.

headline: 4 riders in today's peloton already climbed Sierra de la Pandera in 2017 and 2022
subtext: - Richard Carapaz (14th and 1st) - Enric Mas (51st and 5th) - David de la Cruz (15th ad 24th) - Julien Bernard (81st and 78th)

headline: Carapaz: "When I won, it was a bit different"
subtext: "This stage brings back some lovely memories for me, even though it was a bit different", Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) said at the start. "But I’m always keen to try and repeat the feat; let’s see how the race goes today. After all, when I won, it was a bit different and I was in a different position. I think it’s a tough day; there’ll be a lot more elevation gain. I reckon it’ll be quite a challenging stage, and I hope to be among the best." At the time, the Ecuadorian climber was chasing stages after losing time in the overall standings. He won stages 12 (Peñas Blancas), 14 (Sierra de la Pandera) and 20 (Puerto de Nevacerreda). In 2022, the peloton tackled the Sierra de la Pandera climb from Los Villares while they face the Valdepeñas de Jaén side today, like in 2017, when Rafal Maja won the stage from the early breakaway.

headline: Vermaerke, a tireless attacker
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG) is more than a minute ahead of his breakaway rivals as he enters the final 40 kilometres. He was already in the breakaway en route to Alto de Aitana (stage 9), Calar Alto (stage 12) and Loja (stage 13), and he attacked several times in the finale to Elche de la Sierra (stage 10).

headline: The gap to the peloton increases to 7 minutes
subtext: Will it be enough for the attackers to battle for the stage win up the Puerto de Locubin and then Sierra de la Pandera?

headline: Christophe Laporte has abandoned
subtext: His team Visma-Lease a Bike reported it on their social media.

headline: Vermaerke passes the intermediate sprint and begins the penultimate ascent
subtext: The chasers trail by 1'40'' as the American puncheur tackles the climb up Puerto de Locubin (8.8 km at 5.1%). The gap to the peloton is up to 8 minutes.

headline: Berthet and Rodriguez threaten the GC top 5
subtext: With a gap of 6'20'' from the chasers to the peloton, Clément Berthet (Groupama-FDJ United) and Cristian Rodriguez (XDS Astana) are moving past Harold Tejada (XDS Astana), Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious). They need about twenty more seconds to pass Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos), who started the day in 5th position overall (+4'59'').

headline: 25 kilometres to go for Vermaerke
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG) faces the final 4 kilometres up the Puerto de Locubin with a gap of 1'30'' to his chasers. The peloton trail by 7'50''. Someriders are dropped: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), Yevgenyi Fedorov (XDS Astana)...

headline: The gaps decrease
subtext: But Vermaerke is still 1'10'' ahead of the chase group and 7'35'' of the peloton as he faces the final 2 kilometres up the Puerto de Locubin.

subtext: They have both Lorenzo Fortunato and Cristian Rodriguez to shine at Sierra de la Pandera.

headline: Vermaerke crests the Puerto de Locubin

headline: Results at Puerto de Locubin (cat. 2, km 133.2)
subtext: 1. Vermaerke, 5 pts / 6'' 2. Cr. Rodriguez, 3 pts / 4'' 3. Berthet, 1 pt / 2''

headline: Soon in Valdepeñas de Jaén
subtext: Valdepeñas de Jaén is famed for its steep wall (passed at km 141) that has witnessed La Vuelta stage wins for Igor Antonio (2010), Joaquim Rodriguez (2011), Dani Moreno (2013), and Primoz Roglic (2021). The Slovenian got the better of Enric Mas en route to the third of his four La Vuelta overall victories. Dani Moreno turns 45 years old today.

headline: Steinhauser catches Vermaerke up the wall of Valdepeñas de Jaén
subtext: The other attackers are just behind.

headline: The final climb: Sierra de la Pandera!
subtext: Georg Steinahuser (EF Education-EasyPost) tackles the 11.9 km climb (7.2% on average, with gradients up to 17%) with a smal gap to Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), who is still ahead of the rest of the attackers.

subtext: Zana, Roriguez, Brenner, Buitrago, Paret-peintre and Sosa have accelerated. They are less than 20 seconds behind the lead trio.

Mas and Gall have opened a gap
